stumbles.quote: Colours match a reference at mean ΔE76 0.07.
stumbles.why: The reference is never identified (a photo? a physical film? a thin-film interference model?). Without that, the number can't be interpreted.

stumbles.quote: thick film sinks toward your tilt, thin rises
stumbles.why: It isn't clear what "your tilt" means on a desktop. It also doesn't say what device input drives it. This links to the phone remark, but the text never makes that link.

stumbles.quote: black film spreads from the top
stumbles.why: "Black film" is a soap-bubble term that many developers won't know. The text doesn't explain it, so it reads as an odd colour or a rendering glitch.

stumbles.quote: Not yet tried on a real phone.
stumbles.why: It's unclear why a phone matters here. The text never says the demo needs tilt or a phone, or that it is meant for phones. It also doesn't say whether it runs on desktop, or which browsers support WebGPU.

point: A WebGPU compute-shader soap film simulation, in which thickness acts as density and drives drainage, black-film spread and popping. Its colours were checked against a reference, and the author hasn't tested it on a phone.
